---

A modern, open-source icon library distributed as **webfonts**.  
It provides a curated collection of icons organised by styles, automatically generated from SVG sources, and published as a single npm package (`@bivelicons/webfonts`).

- **Multiple styles** – Solid Rounded, Brands, with more to come.
- **Automated pipeline** – From SVG to webfonts with a single command.
- **Stable & predictable** – Immutable Unicode codepoints, deterministic builds.
- **Lightweight** – Optimised SVGs, WOFF2/WOFF only, minimal CSS.
- **Easy to use** – Simple class-based API, CDN-ready.

## Key files explained

| File / folder                               | Role                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `configs/styles.config.js`                  | Declares every icon style (id, prefix, font name, Unicode block). The single source of truth for all styles.                              |
| `configs/codepoints/`                       | Stores immutable mappings between icon names and their Unicode codepoints. One JSON file per style.                                       |
| `configs/fantasticon/fantasticon.config.js` | Builds the Fantasticon configuration for a given style using the codepoints from the registry.                                            |
| `configs/fantasticon/template.css.hbs`      | Handlebars template that produces the final CSS with `@font-face`, base class, and per‑icon rules.                                        |
| `configs/svgo/svgo.config.js`               | SVGO optimisation rules – removes strokes, converts shapes to paths, normalises structure.                                                |
| `configs/utils/paths.js`                    | Centralised path resolution; all scripts import their directories from here.                                                              |
| `scripts/assign-unicodes.js`                | Scans `src/icons/`, validates names, assigns a permanent Unicode codepoint to each icon, and writes the mapping in `configs/codepoints/`. |
| `scripts/lint-svg.js`                       | Checks XML validity, presence of `viewBox`, absence of strokes, and existence of drawable elements.                                       |
| `scripts/optimize-svg.js`                   | Runs SVGO on every source SVG and writes the result to `packages/optimized/`. Skips files that are already up‑to‑date.                    |
| `scripts/build-fonts.js`                    | Generates WOFF2/WOFF fonts and CSS files using Fantasticon, then assembles the final npm package in `packages/webfonts/`.                 |
| `scripts/utils/os-paths.js`                 | Normalises paths to POSIX format and patches Fantasticon’s glob for Windows compatibility.                                                |
| `turbo.json`                                | Defines the task pipeline (`assign-unicodes → lint-svg → optimize-svg → build-fonts`) and enables caching.                                |

## Build pipeline

The entire transformation from raw SVGs to a publishable npm package is automated by a deterministic pipeline orchestrated with Turborepo.

```text
src/icons/
    │
    ▼
assign-unicodes.js       → validate icon names, allocate immutable Unicode codepoints
    │
    ▼
lint-svg.js              → verify XML structure, viewBox, fill‑only, drawable elements
    │
    ▼
optimize-svg.js          → SVGO optimisation, shape‑to‑path, normalisation
    │
    ▼
build-fonts.js           → Fantasticon generates WOFF2/WOFF + CSS
    │
    ▼
packages/webfonts/       ← final package ready for npm
```

- **Each step is independent** and can be executed separately.
- **Turborepo caches** every step; subsequent builds only re‑run what changed.
- **Fail‑fast**: any error stops the pipeline immediately.

---

## Supported styles

| Style         | Prefix  | Description                       | Icons (v0.1.0) |
| ------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- |
| Solid Rounded | `bi-sr` | Filled icons with rounded corners | 5,059          |
| Brands        | `bi-br` | Official logos and brand marks    | 256            |

New styles can be added by creating a folder in `src/icons/` and a new entry in `styles.config.js` – no pipeline code needs to change.

## Installation & usage

### Démarrage rapide — CDN

Copiez ce template HTML minimal pour commencer immédiatement :

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="fr">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Bivel Icons</title>

    <!-- jsDelivr (all styles CSS recommanded) -->
    <link
      rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@bivelicons/webfonts/css/bivelicons.css"
    />
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Solid Rounded -->
    <i class="bc bi-sr-home"></i>
    <i class="bc bi-sr-user"></i>
    <i class="bc bi-sr-settings"></i>

    <!-- Brands -->
    <i class="bc bs-br-github"></i>
    <i class="bc bs-br-adobe"></i>
    <i class="bc bs-br-apple"></i>
  </body>
</html>
```

### Installation

```bash
# npm

# pnpm
pnpm add @bivelicons/webfonts
```

## CSS API

The class naming convention is:

```md
bc bi-{prefix}-{name}
│ │ │ └── Icon name (kebab‑case, from SVG file)
│ │ └── Style prefix (sr, br)
│ └── Icon namespace
└── Base class (sets font, antialiasing, etc.)
```

- **`bc`** is mandatory on every icon element.
- **`bi-sr-*`** → Solid Rounded icons.
- **`bi-br-*`** → Brands icons.
- Icon names are **lowercase kebab‑case**, exactly matching the source SVG filenames.

---

## Performance

- SVGs are optimised with SVGO before font generation – strokes are stripped, shapes converted to paths, and metadata removed.
- Only **WOFF2** and **WOFF** formats are distributed (96%+ browser coverage).
- CSS files are minimal; the combined `bivelicons.css` includes all styles, while per‑style files allow selective loading.
- Glyphs are normalised to a consistent height, preventing layout shifts.
